pins: progression crosses the eval pass and the funded counters accumulate from zero on a stream that carries no freeze input anywhere, because R-40's context gates are read at request time and INV-23 keeps them out of the replayed state
note: THE COUNTERS ARE THE PIN, AND THEY ARE 2 RATHER THAN 3. Three days are traded and every one of them clears the 15,000c win floor, so an engine that counted from account open reports 3 and 3 here. R-31 zeroes both at the pass and R-33 says the funded count runs 'from the funded reset, not from account open', so the funded phase sees exactly the two days that followed it. `consistency_period_start_day: 2026-11-03` is the same statement from the other side and it is AS-12's boundary applied at funded start rather than at a settlement: the pass day is EXCLUDED from the new period, which is why `consistency_period_profit_cents` is 120,000 and not 420,000. THE WITHDRAWABLE IS 20,000c AND THE ACCOUNT IS NOT ELIGIBLE, which is the pair B4 #15 is about. R-35 puts 20,000c past the buffer, and the win-day gate wants 5 against the 2 this stream reaches, so the engine gates already stop it before any context gate is consulted. That is deliberate: five win days cannot be reached inside a five-session calendar that also has to spend a day passing the eval, so this fixture asserts the accumulation rather than the eligibility, and says so rather than implying a coverage it does not have. THREE FIELDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED AND ADR-050 IS WHY. `floor_cents`, `floor_locked` and `high_water_balance_cents` all depend on whether `floorLocked` carries across the funded reset, which ADR-050 explicitly does NOT rule: R-31 does not name the flag, INV-07 calls a locked floor permanent 'for the life of the account', and progression.ts clears it on a derivation from section 3.4's floor machine that is sound and is still not a ruling. Under 'cleared' the floor trails to 4,810,000 and then 4,870,000 and the high-water balance follows the closes; under 'carried' the floor is frozen at 4,750,000 and the high-water balance is frozen at 5,000,000. EVERY LOW IN THIS STREAM SITS ABOVE BOTH CANDIDATES, so the breach outcome is identical under either reading and the fixture's silence costs it nothing it could otherwise assert. GS-069 declined a floor for the neighbouring reason and this is the same restraint. THE ONE FLOOR THIS SCENARIO COULD HAVE PINNED IS THE RESET ITSELF, 4,750,000c on the pass day, and it is unambiguous for a reason worth recording: the pass day's DO-7 leaves the floor at 5,050,000 under section 3.4's `max` and 5,010,000 under section 3.6's assignment, and DO-8 overwrites both with `size_cents` minus the funded drawdown. THE RESET ERASES THE ONE DISAGREEMENT AND CREATES THE OTHER. GS-019 owns that value; this fixture is about what happens after it. THE EVENT LIST IS DETERMINATE UNDER BOTH READINGS TOO. Neither funded day reaches 260,000c of closing profit, so no second `rule.floor_locked` fires whether the flag carried or not, and no `breach.detected` and no `phase.passed` can appear twice: R-24 makes breach terminal and INV-13 makes the phase move one way.
